decisions.basis: Design §7.7 names the per-row cost precisely: computeKey's string(buf) "escapes" at the function boundary, i.e. one heap allocation per row today. Comparing allocations-per-op between the folded and per-row paths on the same fixture measures exactly that waste using an idiomatic Go testing mechanism, avoiding a new test-only field on BatchAggregation.

decisions.point: Reach: which callers and lifecycle paths depend on BatchAggregation.Consume's current per-row semantics and must remain correct under span-folding.
options: Audit only the standalone part-backed query path
Audit standalone, the distributed data-node map phase, and index-mode's non-streaming aggregator, plus Close/budget-release behaviour
decisions.chosen: Audit standalone + distributed map-phase + index-mode, and Close/budget-release
decisions.basis: BatchAggregation is constructed once by BuildOperators for both standalone GroupByAgg queries and the data-node map phase (AggModeMap) of distributed queries — same operator, same Consume, so a span-folding bug corrupts both deployment shapes identically (the same silent-wrong-number risk class §7.4 calls out for COUNT_DISTINCT). Close is unaffected: folding only changes which rows resolve to an already-created group within one Consume call; it does not change the once-per-group MemoryTracker charge/release in Close (§7.6) since folding reduces re-resolutions of the same group rather than creating new ones, and introduces no new goroutine, I/O, or cancellation-sensitive wait — the span is bounded by the existing maxBlockLength=8192 per-block cap. Risk: no existing test asserts on live group-resolution call counts (only output-row equality is tested today per §11), so the new test must add that assertion itself rather than relying on coverage that doesn't yet exist.

result.title: perf(measure): fold tag-aggregation spans by (series, bucket) instead of per row
result.summary: The vectorized BatchAggregation.Consume operator (pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go) recomputes the group key and re-probes the group map for every row, even when every tag-derived group-by key is index-resolved (an entity or indexed tag that searchSeriesList's three-way projection split already proves constant across one series) and the rows form a contiguous (series, bucket) span — wasting n-1 key computations, map probes, and (for COUNT_DISTINCT) redundant idempotent set inserts per span. The fix adds a plan-time index-resolved flag per group-by key, carried from the analyzer's existing entity/indexed-tag classification into the operator (never inferred at runtime by sampling column values), and changes Consume to resolve the group once per maximal (series, bucket) span — reusing the span boundaries BatchTimeBucket already detects while scanning for bucket advances — whenever every tag-derived key in that span is index-resolved: COUNT becomes count += spanLength and COUNT_DISTINCT becomes one set insert when the aggregation target is also index-resolved, while SUM/MIN/MAX/MEAN keep folding per row but skip the now-redundant key recomputation. This fix is scoped to Phase A (run-folding) only; Phase B (bypassing block decode entirely for a metadata-only scan) is the issue's own next phase, explicitly sequenced "after Phase A lands," and is deferred to a follow-up. No wire format, API, or default-behaviour change is introduced; correctness is pinned by a differential test against the existing, unoptimized per-row path on the same fixture, plus a magnitude assertion on span count.

<result>## Findings: current state of the vectorized aggregation operator (post PR #1360)

The design doc's status line ("design — not implemented") is stale for the parts asked about — all seven pieces exist in code today, largely matching the doc, with a couple of nuances below.

### 1. `BatchAggregation` / `Consume` / `computeKey`
File: `pkg/query/vectorized/measure/aggregation.go`

- `BatchAggregation` struct: lines 132–161 (fields `groups map[string]*aggGroup`, `insertion []*aggGroup`, `keyIndices`, `aggs []AggSpec`, etc.)
- `Consume`: lines 375–421. Per active row it computes `key := a.computeKey(b, int(rowIdx))` (line 387), for `AggModeReduce` checks dedup, then probes `group, exists := a.groups[key]` (line 394), creates `newGroup` on miss (reserving memory), and folds each `AggSpec` via `a.fold(...)` (line 415) or `a.combinePartial(...)` for reduce mode.
- `computeKey` (lines 693–702):
```go
func (a *BatchAggregation) computeKey(b *vectorized.RecordBatch, rowIdx int) string {
	var sb [64]byte
	buf := sb[:0]
	for _, kIdx := range a.keyIndices {
		buf = appendKeyComponent(buf, b.Columns[kIdx], rowIdx)
	}
	return string(buf)
}
```
Confirmed: it **does** allocate a string per row (`string(buf)`), even though `buf` is stack-backed when small — the conversion to `string` copies into a new heap allocation (escape-analysis dependent) on every row, exactly as the design doc says.

### 2. `appendKeyComponent` — `groupby.go:290-306`
```go
func appendKeyComponent(dst []byte, col vectorized.Column, rowIdx int) []byte {
	switch c := col.(type) {
	case *vectorized.TypedColumn[int64]:        return appendIntKey(dst, c.Data()[rowIdx])
	case *vectorized.TypedColumn[float64]:      return appendFloatKey(dst, c.Data()[rowIdx])
	case *vectorized.TypedColumn[string]:       return appendStringKey(dst, c.Data()[rowIdx])
	case *vectorized.TypedColumn[[]byte]:       return appendBytesKey(dst, c.Data()[rowIdx])
	case *vectorized.TypedColumn[*modelv1.TagValue]:   return appendTagValueKey(dst, c.Data()[rowIdx])
	case *vectorized.TypedColumn[*modelv1.FieldValue]: return appendFieldValueKey(dst, c.Data()[rowIdx])
	}
	return dst
}
```
Supports exactly int64/float64/string/[]byte/`*modelv1.TagValue`/`*modelv1.FieldValue`. For any other type (array columns `ColumnTypeInt64Array`/`ColumnTypeStrArray`, etc.) it falls through and **still silently returns `dst` unchanged** — the raw encoder is unfixed. However, a guard the design proposed has since been added alongside it (lines 308–324):
```go
func KeyComponentSupported(t vectorized.ColumnType) bool {
	switch t {
	case vectorized.ColumnTypeInt64, vectorized.ColumnTypeFloat64,
		vectorized.ColumnTypeString, vectorized.ColumnTypeBytes,
		vectorized.ColumnTypeTagValue, vectorized.ColumnTypeFieldValue:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}
```
So the encoder itself is unchanged, but there is now an exported predicate the analyzer consults to reject array/timestamp targets before they ever reach `appendKeyComponent` — the doc's suggested mitigation, implemented as a separate guard rather than a fix to `appendKeyComponent` itself.

### 3. `BatchTimeBucket` bucket-advance detection
File: `pkg/query/vectorized/measure/timebucket.go`, method `consumeBatch` (lines 312–367), streaming branch (lines 337–366):
```go
runStart := 0
for i, rowIdx := range active {
	bucket := tsData[rowIdx]
	switch {
	case !bt.hasBucket:
		... bt.currentBucket = bucket; bt.openBucket(ctx); runStart = i
	case bucket == bt.currentBucket:
		// Same run; keep accumulating.
	case bucket > bt.currentBucket:
		bt.feedRun(ctx, b, active[runStart:i])
		bt.flushCurrentBucket(ctx)
		bt.currentBucket = bucket
		bt.openBucket(ctx)
		runStart = i
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("... input is not time-ascending — row bucket %d precedes the current bucket %d", bucket, bt.currentBucket)
	}
}
return bt.feedRun(ctx, b, active[runStart:])
```
This is the exact run-boundary comparison (`bucket == / > / < bt.currentBucket`) Phase A would reuse for `(series, bucket)` span detection — it already splits a batch into contiguous same-key runs, flushes on advance, and hard-fails on regression (monotonicity guard).

### 4. `collectTagIndices` — `aggregation.go:293-310`
```go
func collectTagIndices(input *vectorized.BatchSchema, keyIndices []int, exclude map[int]struct{}) []int {
	...
	for i, def := range input.Columns {
		if def.Role != vectorized.RoleTag { continue }
		hasTagCols = true
		if _, skip := exclude[i]; skip { continue }
		out = append(out, i)
	}
	...
}
```
Yes — already implemented exactly as the design describes: it takes an `exclude map[int]struct{}` built by `hiddenTagExclusionSet` (lines 316–328) from every `AggSpec.HideTag`, so a hidden target tag is not re-emitted as a first-seen tag.

### 5. `Distinct` / `AggCountDistinct` / `aggSlot.distinct`
`pkg/query/aggregation/distinct.go:27-76` defines `Distinct{Contains, In, Val, Reset}` and `NewDistinct()` backed by `map[string]struct{}` — matches the doc plus an added `Contains` (used to check-before-reserve in `foldDistinct`). There is no standalone `AggCountDistinct` function in this package — `NewMap`/`NewReduce` (`pkg/query/aggregation/aggregation.go:63-102`) still have no `COUNT_DISTINCT` case and fall to `errUnknownFunc`, confirmed. The enum lives as `measure.AggCountDistinct` (`aggregation.go:80`), and the `aggSlot` variant is `distinct aggregation.Distinct` (`aggregation.go:214`), constructed in `newAggSlot` (`aggregation.go:718-723`).

### 6. `fold` — `aggregation.go:590-621`
```go
func (a *BatchAggregation) fold(b *vectorized.RecordBatch, rowIdx int, slot *aggSlot, spec AggSpec) error {
	col := b.Columns[spec.InputCol]
	if col.IsNull(rowIdx) { return nil }
	if spec.Func == AggCountDistinct { return a.foldDistinct(col, rowIdx, slot) }
	colType := a.inputSchema.Columns[spec.InputCol].Type
	if spec.Func == AggCount && colType != vectorized.ColumnTypeInt64 && colType != vectorized.ColumnTypeFloat64 {
		slot.intMap.In(0)
		return nil
	}
	... // numeric read + In(v)
}
```
Confirmed: COUNT over a non-numeric column takes the null-check-only branch (`slot.intMap.In(0)`) without reading/parsing the value; only `AggCountDistinct` must actually read/encode the value.

### 7. `model.MeasureAgg` — `pkg/query/model/model.go:89-95`
```go
type MeasureAgg struct {
	FieldName string
	TagName   string
	TagFamily string
	Func      modelv1.AggregationFunction
	HideTag   bool
}
```
`TagName`, `TagFamily`, `HideTag` all present as documented. There is **no** "index-resolved" / plan-time column-index field on `MeasureAgg` itself — column resolution lives downstream in `AggSpec.InputCol` (vectorized package) via `lookupAggInputColumnIndex` (`plan.go:286`), not on the model struct. Stage 8a's run-folding work would need to add such a field itself; nothing today marks `MeasureAgg` as index-resolved.</result>

<result>## Summary of findings (current HEAD of the worktree)

All line numbers below are from the files as they currently exist; several differ from the design-doc citations (noted inline).

### 1. `searchSeriesList` — `banyand/measure/query.go:314-466`

Yes, the three-way split is still exactly as described. The loop over `mqo.TagProjection` (query.go:324-355) classifies each tag name against `m.schema.GetEntity().GetTagNames()` (→ **entity tag**, offset recorded in `projectedEntityOffsets map[string]int`), then against `is.fieldIndexLocation` (→ **indexed tag**, recorded in `indexProjection []index.FieldKey` + `fieldToValueType map[string]tagNameWithType`), and anything left over is appended to `newTagProjection` (→ **part-resident tag**, the only thing that survives into `mqo.TagProjection` for the block-cursor read path).

The classification maps (`projectedEntityOffsets`, `fieldToValueType`) are **local variables**, used only inside this call to drive `m.buildStoredIndexValue(...)` (query.go:468-504), which folds entity values + decoded indexed-field bytes into one flat `map[common.SeriesID]map[string]*modelv1.TagValue` called `storedIndexValue`. That's the only thing returned/retained — the *classification itself* (which key came from an entity offset vs. an index field) is **discarded** once `storedIndexValue` is built; downstream code (`queryResult`, `blockCursor.copyAllTo/copyTo`, the aggregation/vectorized layer) only ever sees "is this tag name present in `storedIndexValue[sid]`?" (block.go:548, 652, 713, 788) vs. "look in the block's columnFamily" — it can't distinguish entity-resolved from index-resolved after the fact, only resolved-vs-part-resident.

`newTagProjection` is returned from `Query()` (query.go:161) and reassigned onto `mqo.TagProjection` (query.go:189) before being handed to `queryOptions`/`blockCursor.init` (block.go:498-507) — i.e. it is what actually drives which columns get decoded from the part files. The *original* `mqo.TagProjection` is separately kept on `queryResult.tagProjection` (query.go:176, 800) specifically because `copyAllTo`/`copyTo` need the full tag list (to emit `NullTagValue`/index values for tags that aren't block-resident) — see the comment at query.go:243-252 explaining this split is also needed for `BuildBatchSchema`.

### 2. `copyAllTo` — `banyand/measure/block.go:509-620`

Per-tag resolution order inside the tag loop (line 538 `OUTER:` .. 607): for each tag name, first check `indexValue[tagName] != nil` (line 548) → broadcast the single stored entity/index value across all `size` rows (lines 549-555, "indexValue" = the per-series map from `storedIndexValue`). Only if absent does it fall back to scanning `bc.tagFamilies` (the block-resident columnFamily, lines 556-605) for a matching column, decoding via `mustDecodeTagValue`, or emitting `pbv1.NullTagValue` if the column/family isn't found.

### 3. Block selection / range logic

`query.go:594-639` (`searchBlocks`) is just the driver (inits `tstIter`, pulls blocks via `tstIter.nextBlock()`). The actual overlap decision lives in `banyand/measure/part_iter.go`:
- Primary-block (coarse, per-part) level — `loadNextBlockMetadata` line 149: `if pbm.maxTimestamp < pi.minTimestamp || pbm.minTimestamp > pi.maxTimestamp { continue }`
- Per-block level — `findBlock` lines 232-241: `if bm.timestamps.max < pi.minTimestamp { skip }`, `if bm.timestamps.min > pi.maxTimestamp { next series }`

Both are **pure range-overlap tests** (`[min,max] ∩ [queryMin,queryMax] ≠ ∅`), not full-containment — a block partially overlapping the query range is still included wholesale (row-level filtering happens later in `blockCursor.loadData` via `timestamp.FindRange`, block.go:850).

### 4. `blockMetadata` struct — `banyand/measure/block_metadata.go:63-72`

```go
type blockMetadata struct {
    tagFamilies           map[string]*dataBlock
    tagType               tagType
    field                 columnFamilyMetadata
    tagProjection         []model.TagProjection
    timestamps            timestampsMetadata
    seriesID              common.SeriesID
    uncompressedSizeBytes uint64
    count                 uint64
}
```
Confirmed: `seriesID`, `timestamps.min/max` (via `timestampsMetadata`), `count`. Populated per-block in `partIter.readPrimaryBlock` (part_iter.go:184-208, unmarshals a `blockMetadataArray` from the primary index) and copied into `pi.curBlock` in `findBlock` (line 243 `pi.curBlock.copyFrom(bm)`), which becomes `p.curBlock` consumed by `blockCursor.init(p.p, p.curBlock, qo)` at query.go:620.

LSP workspace-symbol search across the whole repo for `metadataOnly`, `runFold`, `spanLength`, `indexResolved`/`IndexResolved` found no matches in `banyand/measure` (or any query-engine code). The only superficially-similar hits are unrelated: `banyand/internal/sidx` has an unrelated `TestBlockScanner_SpanRecordsSkippedBlocks` (counts *skipped* blocks in the secondary-index block scanner, not row run-folding); `banyand/internal/dump/index_resolver.go` has an `IndexResolver` used only by the backup/restore (`dump`) tool, not the live query path. ### 6. `buildIndexQueryResult` — `query.go:506-592`
